## 裁决 — triage

Triage (daily round, 2026-08-24 01:30Z), verbatim:

> lands in `content/docs/guide/layout.md` (published docs face) → `domain:ui` + `pm:queue`, Task. Both claims are measured against the installed contract; **fix the key list (drop tombstoned `icon`, add the three live keys) and the registration-inputs claim against `packages/layout` current source.**

Two false claims in one blockquote: (1) `PageHeaderProps` "declares `title / subtitle / icon / breadcrumb / actions / aria`" — `icon` is an **ADR-0087 D2 `retiredKey` tombstone** on this shape, and three live keys are missing; (2) "`page-header`'s registration declares **only** `title` and `subtitle`" — `packages/layout/src/index.ts:121` declares four.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not inherit

1. ⛔ **The card's own evidence has a trap in it, and copying the card is how you fall in.** Its measurement quotes `safeParse` **output keys** — `["title","subtitle","breadcrumb","recordChrome","showStar","showCopyId"]` — and from that concludes "the guide omits `recordChrome`, `showStar`, `showCopyId`". That conclusion is right. But **an output-key list is not a declared-key list**: it shows the keys present *after defaults are applied*, so an optional key with no default never appears. Note that `actions` and `aria` are absent from that output while the sibling reference page `content/docs/layout/page-header.mdx` lists both. ⛔ If you write the guide's new list from the card's output keys, you will silently **delete two live keys**. Derive the list from the **shape's declared keys** (walk the zod shape / the type, not one parse result), and show both readings side by side in your report so the difference is on the record.
2. ⚠️ **`icon` is not simply absent — it is a tombstone with a message.** The parser rejects it by name with an ADR-0087 D2 explanation. So "drop `icon`" is not the whole edit: state *why* it is gone where a reader who has `icon` in an existing schema will see it, rather than leaving them to rediscover the parse failure. ⛔ Do not invent the retirement rationale — quote the tombstone's own message.
3. ⚠️ **Claim 2's defect is the word "only".** `packages/layout/src/index.ts:121` declares `title`, `subtitle`, `icon`, `actions`, and the registration's own comment cites objectui#3829 and objectui#3972 as renderer-read-point evidence. Re-derive that list from current source — the card measured it, but `packages/layout` may have moved since 01:12Z today. ⚠️ Note the awkwardness you are about to document and do **not** paper over it: `icon` is a **retired key on the spec shape** and simultaneously a **declared registration input**. If that is genuinely the state of the tree, say so plainly in the guide; if your measurement says otherwise, ⛔ stop and report — that would be a contract finding, not a docs fix.
4. ⚠️ **Nothing mechanically judges this file, so your derivation *is* the verification.** The card establishes it: neither claim is in a code fence, so `check-doc-component-types` and `check-doc-snippet-types` are structurally blind, and `content/docs/guide/layout.md` is additionally in `check-doc-snippet-types`' `UNGATED_DOCS` debt list. ⚠️ Therefore a green CI run is **not** evidence your new text is true — it is only evidence you broke nothing. Say that explicitly in the report rather than letting green stand in for correctness.

## PM建议路线 — and a route the card leaves open that you ⛔ may not take

Fix **in place**, and add a pointer to `content/docs/layout/page-header.mdx` as the reference face. The card's "Suggested shape" wonders *"whether the two lists belong on the guide at all"* — ⛔ **do not delete the lists.** That is a docs-structure decision the card explicitly declines to take and this dispatch does not grant. If, having done the fix, you think deletion is the better end state, ✅ say so in the report with your reasoning and leave it for a ruling.

## Verification

Predict the direction **before** running. Prove the edit on disk by grepping the **injected** text and, **separately**, the **removed** text — for this card that means the retired `icon` mention is gone from the claim-1 list, the three live keys are present, and the word `only` is gone from claim 2. ⚠️ Print the landing site; ⚠️ assert anchor uniqueness before writing (this blockquote's phrasing may well appear elsewhere in the file); ⚠️ restore any probe mutation under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with a **cwd-independent** command and confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` shows only your intended file. Every zero-hit grep needs a known-present control.

**Gates by name, with exit codes:** `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` (⚠️ a docs-only change under `content/docs/` may legitimately owe **no** changeset — quote the gate's own verdict line either way; if one is owed, this repo accepts **empty frontmatter** as the explicit "releases nothing" declaration), `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`, `node scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs`, `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs`, and `check:doc-snippets` — ⚠️ for that last one **state its verdict *and* its blindness**: report whether this file is inside its scan surface at all, quoting the script's own `DOCS_ROOT` constant and the `UNGATED_DOCS` entry, rather than reporting a pass that means nothing here. ⚠️ If eslint does not lint this path, say so **by quoting the config that excludes it**, ⛔ not by your own judgement that prose needs no linting.

## Deliverable

Draft PR, body with `Fixes #5923`. ⛔ Do not mark ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ no auto-merge — the PM lands it. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — they render as HTML and vanish) and return it. State, per gate: command, exit code, what a red would have meant, **and for the doc gates, what a green does not mean**; plus the measured answer to each of assumptions 1–4 and any deviation with its reason.

## Measured answers to PM mechanism assumptions 1-4

**1 — CONFIRMED, and the trap was real.** Both readings side by side, against installed `@objectstack/spec` **17.2.0** (the version this branch's `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves; read from an already-installed copy of the identical version, then re-confirmed after installing in my own worktree):

| reading | result |
|---|---|
| card's `safeParse` **output** keys for `{title, subtitle}` | `title, subtitle, breadcrumb, recordChrome, showStar, showCopyId` — **6** |
| **declared** keys, walking the zod shape | `title, subtitle, icon, breadcrumb, actions, recordChrome, showStar, showCopyId, maxVisible, mobileMaxVisible, aria` — **11 entries, 10 live + the icon tombstone** |

Writing the guide from the card's output list would have deleted `actions` and `aria` exactly as predicted, **and** would never have surfaced `maxVisible` / `mobileMaxVisible` — two live keys the card did not know about and which the sibling reference page also omits. Feeding all ten live keys in at once returns all ten in the output, which is the control proving the short list was an artifact of the input, not of the contract. Negative control `{title, zzzNotAKey}` still rejects with `unrecognized_keys`, so the shape is strict and these readings mean something.

**2 — CONFIRMED; message quoted, not invented.** `icon` is `optional -> never` in the shape — the tombstone lives *in* the shape, which is why it rejects with `invalid_type path=["icon"]` rather than `unrecognized_keys`. The guide now carries the tombstone's own words: "`page:header` property `icon` was removed in @objectstack/spec 17.0.0 (#6946, ADR-0087 D2) — no renderer ever read it … Delete the key."

**3 — CONFIRMED against current source; the awkwardness is real and is documented, not papered over.** `packages/layout/src/index.ts:121` registers `page-header`; `:126-136` declares four inputs — `title`, `subtitle`, `icon`, `actions`. Unchanged since the card was filed. This is **not** a contract finding: the registration's own comment explains the split, and it is coherent. `PageHeaderProps.icon` was retired upstream because the **canonical** `page:header` renderer never read it; `@object-ui/layout`'s `PageHeader` **does** draw it beside the title (read at `PageHeader.tsx:123`, rendered at `:231-233`), which objectui#3829 ruled it keeps, and `page-header-authorable-keys.test.tsx` skips tombstones when deriving the spec key set so the retired key cannot read as parity. Different renderers, opposite read facts. The guide now says so plainly.

**4 — CONFIRMED in conclusion, but one premise is STALE.** The conclusion holds: neither claim is in a code fence, and `check-doc-snippet-types` compiles only `TS_FENCE_LANGUAGES = ["ts","tsx","typescript"]`, so both doc gates are structurally blind to this edit. **A green run is not evidence the new prose is true — only that nothing broke. The derivation above is the verification.** The stale premise: `content/docs/guide/layout.md` is **no longer** in `UNGATED_DOCS`. Read at runtime, that map holds 44 entries and this file is not among them; the run reports "178 covered, 44 ungated" and this file sits in the covered set. It is covered at document level and still fence-blind to prose — so the right conclusion, for a different reason than the card gave. (A textual scrape of the constant gave me 12 entries; the runtime read of 44 is the authoritative one and corrected my own first measurement.)

**eslint** does not lint this path, per the config rather than my judgement: the only rule-bearing block in `eslint.config.js` is scoped `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']`, so a `.md` file matches no configuration. eslint's own output on the file: "File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied."

## Gate-set derivation and deviations

Gate set derived by enumerating each workflow's own step list, not from top-level script names. The doc gates each live in their own standalone workflow (`changeset-presence.yml`, `docs-links.yml`, `doc-component-types.yml`, `control-bytes.yml`, `doc-snippet-types.yml`); `ci.yml:1157-1175` carries an explicit "do not add it back" note pinning `check-doc-links.mjs` to exactly one home, so no doc gate hides inside an unrelated job. `content/**` appears in `ci.yml`, `lint.yml` and `live-e2e.yml` only as `paths-ignore` on the **push** trigger.

**Deviations: none.** The lists were kept as instructed, nothing outside `content/docs/guide/layout.md` was written, `content/docs/releases/` was not touched, the PR is draft and was not marked ready or enqueued, and no `skip-changeset` label was created or applied in this repo (that mechanism does not exist here, and the gate says no changeset is owed, so no empty-frontmatter changeset was needed either).

## PM review — **ACCEPT**, enqueued

PR **#6082** at `675d333a9`. Gates read **once** at 16:25Z, armed off this run's own `started_at` (16:12:54Z).

**19 checks, 16 success + 3 skipped, 0 failing, 0 still running.** ⚠️ Read honestly: this is *every check that ran*, and a docs-only diff triggers fewer jobs than a code diff — `Bundle Analysis`, `Live E2E` and `Changeset Bump Policy` are absent here where a code PR has them. Path-conditional, not missing. Not a governed surface (`content/docs/guide/`, not `docs/adr/**` or `skills/**`), so: marked ready, enqueued through the merge queue; ⛔ nothing merged by hand.

### The trap was real, and it was bigger than I priced it

I flagged that the card's evidence is a `safeParse` **output-key** list and that copying it would delete `actions` and `aria`. The dev measured it: **the declared-key walk gives 11 (10 live + the `icon` tombstone); the card's output-key reading gives 6.** So copying the card would have deleted two live keys *and* never surfaced `maxVisible` / `mobileMaxVisible` — two keys that were undocumented on **both** pages. ✅ Derived from the zod shape, not from a parse result, with both readings put side by side in the report. That is the whole card.

### The finding that kills the obvious cleanup

**#6083** — `content/docs/layout/page-header.mdx:66-68` omits `maxVisible` and `mobileMaxVisible`. ⚠️ This matters beyond its own card: the sibling reference page was the copy this fix was written to defer to, and **it was also wrong**. "Consolidate onto one copy" would have consolidated onto an incorrect one. There was no correct copy anywhere in the tree.

### Assumptions, as measured

1. **Confirmed, and load-bearing** — see above.
2. Not disputed: the `icon` tombstone's own ADR-0087 D2 message is quoted rather than a rationale invented.
3. **Confirmed — and it is NOT a contract finding.** `packages/layout/src/index.ts:126-136` declares four inputs, and the `icon` split is coherent once you see there are two renderers: the canonical `page:header` renderer never read `icon` (hence the upstream retirement), while `@object-ui/layout`'s `PageHeader` **does** draw it. Opposite read facts, different components. The guide now states that plainly instead of papering over it. ✅ Right call not to stop-and-report on an apparent contradiction that resolves under measurement.
4. **Conclusion holds, one premise was stale.** `content/docs/guide/layout.md` is **no longer** in `UNGATED_DOCS` (44 entries at runtime; this file is among the covered 178). ⚠️ Being *inside* the scan surface bought nothing — the gates are fence-shaped and the prose sits outside a fence — so "green means nothing broke, the derivation is the verification" still stands. ✅ Correcting a premise of its own dispatch rather than repeating it is exactly what these assumptions are for.

### Verification hygiene worth recording

Anchor uniqueness asserted **before** writing (both anchors exactly 1 occurrence; repo-wide grep for the key-list anchor returned only line 290 — this is the trap that bit #5927 this round). Removed and injected text grepped **separately**, each prediction stated first, all met, with known-present controls (`PageHeaderProps` still 2, the `/docs/layout/page-header` pointer still 2). `git diff HEAD --stat` exactly one file. Worktree removed **without** `--force`, which is itself evidence nothing uncommitted was left behind.

⚠️ One gate reading worth keeping: `check-doc-snippet-types` first exited **1** with *"The snippet program was NOT run: the packages it resolves against are not built"* — an unbuilt tree, ⛔ not a defect in the change. Resolved by running the workflow's own steps (`--build-filter`, then `turbo run build` over the 20 packages it names, 32/32 successful) **before** re-reading. ✅ A red that means "the instrument did not run" is not the same as a red that means "your change is wrong", and the report distinguishes them.

### The open question — routed, not answered

The dev asks whether the guide should keep its two lists at all, recommending **A (keep) now, C (a mechanical judge) as the durable fix**, and rejecting B (defer to the reference page) on the grounds above — the reference page was not a correct copy either. ✅ I agree with that reasoning and it is why B is off the table.

**C is now filed as #6086** — the class, not the instance: prose restating a declared surface has no mechanical judge in this repo, every doc gate being fence-shaped. It carries the two traps a naive implementation walks into, both measured here: declared keys ≠ `safeParse` output keys (a gate built on the latter would have *demanded* the deletion of `actions`/`aria`, enforcing the very defect it exists to catch), and a retired key must stay distinguishable from an absent one.

A-vs-B needed no maintainer ruling — A is the status quo and the PR ships it; ⛔ deletion was correctly not taken.

## Board correction: `pm:dispatched` → `pm:awaiting-maintainer`. ⛔ No new diagnosis, no work lost.

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`.

### What was wrong with the label

The card read `pm:dispatched` — *"a dev is working on this"* — for roughly 30 hours after the dev
finished. The work is **delivered**: PR #6082, head `b12ed7be0`, 24 checks green,
`mergeable_state: clean`, zero review threads. Nothing is in flight and no agent holds the branch.

⚠️ **This is not cosmetic. It misread as a live claim twice today, including once by me** — a
`pm:dispatched` card with an assignee is exactly what an in-flight census is looking for, so the
card kept presenting itself as work-in-progress while the real state was "finished, stuck,
waiting on a person." Those two states must not look alike on the board.

### Why `pm:awaiting-maintainer` and not `pm:blocked`

`pm:blocked` wants a machine-readable `Blocked-by: #N` pointing at an upstream card the unlock
scan can watch close. **There is no such card here.** The remaining action is a single human
operation outside the issue surface — someone with repository-settings read looking at why a
green, clean, conflict-free PR will not merge. `pm:awaiting-maintainer` is the state written for
exactly that, and it is mutually exclusive with the other `pm:*` states, so `pm:dispatched` comes
off in the same write. (A `pm:blocked` with no `Blocked-by:` line is invisible to the unlock scan
— I repaired one of those on #5950 earlier today and am not creating another.)

### The action this card is waiting on

**A maintainer with repository-settings / branch-protection read** determines why PR #6082 does
not merge. Everything an execution seat can measure has been measured.

### ⛔ Do not open a fifth diagnosis

Four have been raised on PR #6082 and **all four were falsified or retracted**, each by the seat
that raised it:

1. a repository-settings problem — withdrawn by its own author;
2. the old head carrying no commit status — falsified with a pre-declared control;
3. the fourth auto-merge attempt — abandoned as "repeating a failed action is not a diagnosis";
4. the unexpanded `Test (coverage shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)` matrix placeholder — **mine**,
   retracted 40 minutes after I raised it, when the control I had skipped showed the identical
   skipped row on PRs that merge perfectly well.

⭐ The standing instruction from the outgoing seat is explicit and I am carrying it forward:
**no fifth diagnosis.** The failure mode here is not a missing insight, it is four seats in a row
substituting a plausible mechanism for a measurement. The next step is access, not another
hypothesis.

Auto-merge stays **off** (disabled at 07:54Z), deliberately: with it on, the PR reads as "queued,
merging shortly" when it is actually "escalated, waiting on a human", and this lane has already
spent a night on that exact ambiguity.

### Attribution for this label change

Made by this seat, on its own reading of the state machine — not on anyone's instruction. The
evidence is above and the change is reversible: if a maintainer judges `pm:blocked` the better
state, moving it back costs one write.
